studies.classification: mixed: engine collision behaviour; local explanatory prediction and open-plane update
engineSteps: scene-engine avoid returns the actual acceleration, including its fixed 1.5 s window, existing-overlap branch and zero-vector normalisation behaviour.
Engine vector operations perform relative arithmetic, speed clipping and vector normalisation.
localSteps: closestApproach exposes signed dot-product time and both projected centres on every frame.
Fixed-step integration advances the courier with updated capped velocity and advances the porter at unchanged velocity.
minimumCollisionSeparation checks linear relative travel between fixed samples for the comparison finding.
claimsCoveredByAuthoredSpecs: Initial time 1.25 s, predicted gap 1 unit, contact distance 2 units and downward acceleration 6 units/s².
Past approach, equal-velocity, safe-gap and exact-horizon rejection; existing-overlap response.
Default pass retains positive physical clearance, including travel between samples.
Changing only porterStartY to zero exposes initial zero steering and subsequent body overlap.
Every selected frame supplies the closest-approach text and projected-centre coordinates; chart series and projection links cover the same run.
Determinism and comparison equality when the editable offset equals the comparison offset.
limitations: Only the courier steers, against one coasting neighbour; no reciprocal crowd policy or destination is supplied.
The 1.5 s horizon is fixed in the engine and a differing parameter is refused rather than presented as tunable.
The exact-head-on comparison intentionally preserves the engine zero-direction failure; there is no new tie-break or collision response.
gdx-ai 1.8.2 uses a scalar minimum-separation estimate in its acceptance filter; the record states this explicitly and does not claim it uses the local vector-distance test.

studies.classification: mixed: local finite-ray detector and avoidance-target construction; engine Seek motor
engineSteps: Engine seek computes the actual acceleration towards either the avoidance target or the delivery point.
Engine vector operations normalise direction and clip updated speed.
localSteps: castWallRay intersects finite ray and wall segments with cross products and derives a surface normal opposed to the incoming ray.
A hit target is hit point plus unit normal times avoidDistance; a miss selects the original delivery point.
The fixed-step open-plane update retains last travel heading at rest and applies no wall clamp.
For the central vertical-wall approach, the timeline measures wallX minus centreX minus radius. Rays are drawn as MotionLink records.
claimsCoveredByAuthoredSpecs: Oblique ray intersection fractions and hit coordinates, unit normal orientation, reverse-side normals and endpoint hits.
Finite-range, behind-ray, off-end, parallel and collinear misses; the centre-ray edge-grazing limitation.
The normal-offset target actually changes engine Seek from forward pull to backward pull; hand-worked braking step gives velocity 3.2 and next x 4.72.
The default run remains on the courtyard side but does not find a route around the wall.
Changing only rayLength to 1 makes the disc overlap the wall before its centre crosses; no physics clamp hides this.
All per-frame text placeholders, ray links, bounds, chart lengths and deterministic comparison behaviour.
limitations: One centre ray is not a swept-disc collision test and can miss an endpoint the physical radius clips.
The detector returns no hit for parallel or collinear segments; this boundary is stated and specified.
The symmetric local target pull supplies no route around a wall end and may keep switching targets.
Corner trap is linked as a nearby concept and sourced through gdx-ai commentary, but no multi-ray corner remedy is claimed or executed.
Signed clearance is specifically the courtyard-side measure for this central approach to a vertical segment.

observedClaims: Configured rays are updated and passed to a collision detector; the hit nearest the owner is retained.
